stories.headline: US reimposes Iran naval blockade and bombs military bases, killing 7; Iran declares Hormuz shut

key_facts.fact: The US reimposed a naval blockade on Iran and intensified its airstrike campaign on Wednesday July 15; strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killed at least seven troops and wounded more than 260 people, Iranian officials said.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. reimposed a naval blockade on Iran and intensified its airstrike campaign Wednesday in retaliation for Tehran's attacks on ships trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The American strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killed at least seven troops and wounded more than 260 people across the country, Iranian officials said.

key_facts.fact: The naval blockade against vessels transiting to and from Iranian ports came back into effect at 2000 GMT (1600 EDT) on July 14, after being lifted in June.
key_facts.excerpt: The naval blockade against vessels transiting to and from Iranian ports and coastal areas came back into effect at 2000 GMT (1600 EDT), after being lifted in June.

key_facts.fact: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed; Brent crude rose above $86 a barrel and WTI above $80 as the confrontation deepened supply disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude settled at its highest level since June 12 for a second consecutive session... Brent rising $1.46, or 1.72%, to $86.19 a barrel while WTI gained $1.11, or 1.4%, to $80.40 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: Trump threatened to strike Iran's power plants and bridges next week unless Tehran returns to negotiations, and scrapped the planned 20% levy on ships using the Strait of Hormuz, replacing it with trade deals with Gulf allies.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump warned... threatened to widen strikes next week to hit power plants and bridges unless Tehran returns to the negotiating table... Trump, meanwhile, said he was scrapping a planned levy on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz that he announced on July 13, replacing the fee with trade deals with Gulf allies.

key_facts.fact: At least 30 people have been killed in Iran since renewed US attacks began last week, according to an Iranian government spokesman.
key_facts.excerpt: Since last week, renewed US attacks have killed at least 30 people in Iran, government spokesman Fatemeh Mohajerani said.

stories.headline: US inflation cools sharply in June, collapsing market bets on a July Fed rate hike

key_facts.fact: Headline CPI fell 0.4% in June, the largest monthly decline since April 2020, lowering the annual inflation rate to 3.5% from 4.2% in May; core CPI was flat on the month and eased to 2.6% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: Headline CPI: -0.4% MoM Seasonally Adjusted (SA)—the largest monthly decline since April 2020; annual rate fell to 3.5%, down from 4.2% in May. Core CPI (less food & energy): 0.0% MoM (SA); annual rate fell to 2.6%, down from 2.9% in May, beating forecasts.

key_facts.fact: CME FedWatch odds of a July 29 rate hike fell from 47% to 17% within minutes of the release, with the 10-year Treasury yield down about 6 basis points.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points on release, and the CME FedWatch Tool, which had priced the odds of a July 29 rate hike at 47% just yesterday afternoon, saw those odds fall to 17% minutes after the CPI release.

key_facts.fact: Gasoline prices fell 9.7% month over month, the primary driver of the headline decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Gasoline: -9.7% MoM (SA), +26.7% YoY—the primary driver of the monthly decline

key_facts.fact: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told Congress in his semiannual testimony that the FOMC held the federal funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% at its June meeting and has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.'
key_facts.excerpt: we decided to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.5 to 3.75 percent... The members of our Committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.

stories.headline: Big US banks smash Q2 profit records; JPMorgan earns $21.2B, Goldman jumps 9%

key_facts.fact: Four of the largest US banks reported a collective $43 billion in second-quarter profits on Tuesday July 14, smashing records and exceeding analysts' projections.
key_facts.excerpt: four of the largest banks in the United States reported a collective $43 billion in profits in the second quarter, smashing records and exceeding analysts' projections, despite the war with Iran, stubborn inflation and mounting concerns about the staying power of the artificial intelligence boom.

key_facts.fact: JPMorgan Chase reported Q2 net income of $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share, up from $15.0 billion ($5.24) a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 14, 2026, JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported 2026 second quarter net income of $21.2 billion, or $7.70 per share, compared with net income of $15.0 billion, or $5.24 per share, in the second quarter of 2025.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs reported net earnings of $6.63 billion and diluted EPS of $20.98, a 23.5% annualized return on equity, and raised its quarterly dividend to $5.00 per share; its stock rose 9% on the day.
key_facts.excerpt: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. today reported net revenues of $20.34 billion and net earnings of $6.63 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Diluted earnings per common share (EPS) was $20.98 and annualized return on average common shareholders' equity (ROE) was 23.5%.

key_facts.fact: Citigroup net income rose 45% year over year to $5.8 billion ($3.15 per share) on revenues of $24.8 billion, driven by growth across its five businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: New York, July 14, 2026 - Citigroup Inc. today reported net income for the second quarter 2026 of $5.8 billion, or $3.15 per diluted share, on revenues of $24.8 billion. This compares to net income of $4.0 billion, or $1.96 per diluted share... Net income was $5.8 billion, compared to $4.0 billion in the prior-year period.

stories.headline: Stripe and Advent make joint $53B+ bid for PayPal at $60.50 a share

key_facts.fact: Payments company Stripe and private equity firm Advent International made a joint offer to acquire PayPal for $60.50 per share, valuing it at more than $53 billion and representing about a 28% premium to PayPal's Tuesday close.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe and Advent International have made a joint offer to acquire PayPal Holdings Inc for $60.50 per share, in a deal that would value the payments company at more than $53 billion... represents around a 28 per cent premium to PayPal's closing share price on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: The offer, submitted earlier this month, is backed by about $50 billion in committed bank financing and follows an initial approach in early April.
key_facts.excerpt: The offer, submitted earlier this month, is backed by about $50 billion in committed financing from banks... The proposal follows an initial approach made in early April.

key_facts.fact: Stripe and Advent would jointly own PayPal with equal stakes rather than break it up, and had not yet received a response from PayPal.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe and Advent would jointly own PayPal, with each holding an equal stake, rather than breaking up the company... Stripe and Advent have not received a response from PayPal and are seeking to advance discussions in the coming weeks.

stories.headline: Uber in advanced talks to take over Germany's Delivery Hero, valued above €12B

key_facts.fact: Delivery Hero confirmed on July 14 that it is in advanced negotiations with Uber Technologies over a potential takeover offer to all shareholders.
key_facts.excerpt: Berlin, July 14, 2026 - Delivery Hero SE confirms advanced negotiations with Uber Technologies, Inc. with respect of a potential takeover offer to all shareholders of the Company.

key_facts.fact: Delivery Hero shares closed 5.76% higher at €39.10, giving it a market capitalization of roughly €11.2 billion ($12.8 billion); the deal is expected to value it well above its recent ~€36 share price.
key_facts.excerpt: The Berlin-based firm has seen its value climb by about 62% this year, giving it a market capitalization of roughly 11.2 billion euros ($12.8 billion)... Delivery Hero's stock closed 5.76% higher at 39.10 euros.

key_facts.fact: Uber already holds a 24.99% stake plus derivatives that bring its economic interest to about 36.8%, after a previous approach of €33 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber has already built a significant stake in Delivery Hero, holding 24.99% of the company's shares and additional derivatives that bring its total economic interest to about 36.8%... Uber previously approached the company with an offer of €33 per share.

stories.headline: FDA approves Celcuity's Revtorpyk for advanced breast cancer, a win over Novartis and Roche

key_facts.fact: On July 14 the FDA approved Celcuity's gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) in combination with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for HR-positive, HER2-negative, PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer after at least one line of endocrine therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 14, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) in combination with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for the treatment of adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer without a PIK3CA mutation detected.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 trial, the gedatolisib-plus-fulvestrant doublet cut the risk of disease progression or death by 67% versus fulvestrant alone, while the triplet adding palbociclib cut it by 76%.
key_facts.excerpt: Revtorpyk, also known as gedatolisib, reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 67% in combination with fulvestrant, compared to fulvestrant alone... Patients in that group achieved a 76% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.

key_facts.fact: Celcuity, a small public biotech, positioned the drug to improve on similar treatments from Novartis and Roche; CEO Brian Sullivan wants it to become a 'new standard of care' in second-line HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
key_facts.excerpt: A small public biotech won approval for a breast cancer drug that was designed to improve on similar treatments from Novartis and Roche... Sullivan said... he wants to make Revtorpyk a 'new standard of care' for second-line HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

stories.headline: Daniel Ek's Neko Health raises $700M for preventive full-body scans ahead of US launch

key_facts.fact: Neko Health, the Stockholm health-tech startup co-founded by Spotify's Daniel Ek, announced a $700 million Series C on July 15, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by O.G. Venture Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Neko Health today announced the completion of its $700 million Series C funding round. The round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by O.G. Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors Atomico, General Catalyst, and Lakestar.

key_facts.fact: The round follows a $260 million Series B in January 2025 and drew backers including Atomico, General Catalyst, Lakestar, Liberty City Ventures and BDT & MSD.
key_facts.excerpt: alongside new backers including Liberty City Ventures, Positive Sum, and BDT & MSD. The fundraise follows a $260 million Series B in January 2025.

key_facts.fact: Neko operates eight clinics in Sweden and Britain offering a 60-minute non-invasive full-body scan plus a blood test (priced at £299 in the UK) and plans to open its first US clinics, including in New York, this year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, which operates eight clinics in Sweden and Britain and advertises its service as 'a health check for your future self,' offers full-body diagnostic scans - plus a blood test... A Neko Health scan in Britain is priced at 299 pounds ($400).
